spec.name: purview-contest
spec.intent:
Census @dd055a7b (main); re-derive any line cited below if its path changed since.
Realize on the purview guard the clause of `enforcement scope` as amended 2026-10-01T04:27: a refusal never strands the agent; every refusal leaves it a way to continue on its own; a retry is judged again rather than waved through, and an agent that holds a refusal wrong contests it by stating why, the contested act then proceeding and the contest recorded for the operator to review, never left waiting on the operator. Realize too, on the purview worker, the note 'guard workers are bloated' (topic enforcement scope): a guard is a small act (read the event, decide whether it applies, ask the judge, relay the verdict), and its shell is cut to what that act needs.
AT CENSUS. The cell is packages/canon/src/hooks/purview-guardrail.ts (worker content L74-316, judge prompt L328-351); `pnpm canon:project:targets` projects it to packages/canon/targets/guardrail/purview-guardrail.sh (15407 bytes, 7915 of them in comment lines) and purview-judge-prompt.md (1908). The cell imports `stanceGuardrailJudgeClip` from ./stance-guardrail.js (L2, interpolated at L220) and packages/canon/test/purview-guardrail.test.ts imports `stanceGuardrailJudgeCap` from the same module (L38); both are defined in packages/canon/src/hooks/stance-guardrail.ts (`judgePayloadCapBytes` L20, `judgeClipShell` L29-66, exported L999-1000). The deny (.sh L267-278) relays the judge's reason inside a paragraph of exceptions and offers no way forward beyond complying; the header (.sh L26) and the cell comment (L49) and residue state the retry law as 'a refused act stays refused'. Every file `src/hooks/*.ts` is loaded as a hook cell (packages/canon/tooling/project-targets.ts L62-68; packages/canon/test/reader-density.test.ts L247), so a shared module cannot live in that directory.
CONTEST CONTRACT (the plan's own and stated only here; unit stance-contest cites it from this unit. This unit builds it into packages/canon/src/guard-shell.ts as `contestShell`, the one fragment every guard worker interpolates):
(1) On every refusal (a deny before a call, a block at the turn end) the guard records the judge's reason in `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guardrail-contest/<cell id>/<session>/<key>.refused`, creating the directory, where <key> is the cksum of the call's tool_name and compact tool_input for a call and `stop` at the turn end, and a session id that is not one path segment is read as `nosession`. The reason the guard returns is the judge's reason followed by the way forward: act on that reason, or, if the agent holds the refusal wrong, write why into `<same dir>/<key>.contest` with the one shell command the reason spells out in full (absolute path), then repeat the same call (at the turn end: end the turn again).
(2) A fire for which a non-empty `<key>.contest` exists in its session is NOT judged: the guard appends one line to the contest log, removes that `.contest` and `.refused`, says (through the worker's own `say`, so each harness gets its form) one line naming the guard, that the contested act went through unjudged, the agent's reason and the log's path, and exits 0 with no refusal.
(3) A fire with no contest file is judged as before; a repeat of a refused act with no contest is judged again and refused again on a BLOCK.
(4) The contest log is `$GUARD_CONTEST_LOG`, else `<neutral root>/guardrail/contests.log`, the `.agents` root each worker already derives for its rubric (so `~/.agents/guardrail/contests.log` on both harnesses). Each line is one JSON object with exactly the keys `time` (UTC ISO-8601), `guard` (the cell id), `session`, `agent`, `act` (the tool name, or `stop`), `refusal` (the recorded reason, "" when none was recorded) and `contest` (the agent's reason), written with jq. A log that cannot be written never holds the act back: the act still goes through and the notice says the contest was not recorded.
(5) Nothing the agent runs to contest is refused by a guard: the stance workers judge no shell call and no file write, and the purview worker lets a write or edit whose path lies under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guardrail-contest/` through unjudged.
WHY A FILE AND NOT THE AGENT'S PROSE (census, observed once): on Claude Code 2.1.285 (`claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --settings <a file binding one PreToolUse hook>`), a hook that copied its `transcript_path` at fire time held only the user prompt; the assistant's text block and its tool_use were written after the hook ran. So a contest stated in the message carrying the call cannot reach a pre-call guard, while a file reaches both harnesses with no change to the omp bridge, which already relays any non-JSON worker line from either pass (packages/forge/src/adapters/omp/render.ts L1157-1160 and L1193-1196 at dd055a7b) and is not changed by this plan.
CHANGE. (a) Create packages/canon/src/guard-shell.ts, the one home of the shell every guard worker shares, exporting `judgePayloadCapBytes` and `judgeClipShell` (copied from stance-guardrail.ts at dd055a7b: the clip's comments may be cut, its shell behaviour may not) and `contestShell`, the CONTEST CONTRACT as one fragment that relies on the interpolating worker's own `say` and on variables the worker sets for its cell id, its display name, the session, the agent and the act (name them; unit stance-contest will interpolate the same fragment into both stance workers). (b) The purview cell and its test import these from guard-shell.ts and nothing from stance-guardrail.js. (c) The purview worker honours the contract, and its deny reason is the judge's reason followed by the way forward; any further text stays only where the agent needs it to act. Its residue states the contest in place of the 'stays refused' law. (d) Cut the worker to what its act needs: a comment only where a line cannot say why itself, the history of how a line came to be left to git. What the judge is handed stays byte-identical for the same input; the scope gate, the subagent skip, the contract read, the evidence check and the rubric file stay; each fail-open notice may shorten but still names PURVIEW GUARDRAIL and says the call was NOT judged. (e) Change no stance file (stance-guardrail.ts, stance-guardrail-pre.ts, their targets and tests): unit stance-workers-lean owns them in this wave, and unit stance-contest moves the stance workers onto guard-shell.ts after it. Add .changeset/purview-contest.md (@cratylus/canon patch).
accept: CONTEST: new cases in packages/canon/test/purview-guardrail.test.ts, for each harness form, in the architect's scope, with STANCE_JUDGE_CMD naming a stub that counts its calls and answers `VERDICT: BLOCK` with a REASON and an `EVIDENCE:` span present in the payload, and TMPDIR and GUARD_CONTEST_LOG under a temp dir: (a) a `Task` dispatch to implementer carrying a spec is denied, its deny reason contains the absolute path `<TMPDIR>/guardrail-contest/purview-guardrail/<session>/<key>.contest`, and the sibling `<key>.refused` holds the judge's REASON; (b) after `the unit is routed by name` is written to that path, the identical fire exits 0 with no deny, prints the harness's notice naming PURVIEW GUARDRAIL and containing `the unit is routed by name`, the stub's count is unchanged, GUARD_CONTEST_LOG holds exactly one line whose JSON keys are exactly time, guard, session, agent, act, refusal, contest with guard `purview-guardrail`, act the fired tool name, refusal the judge's REASON and contest the written text, and the `.contest` file is gone; (c) a third identical fire is judged (count +1) and denied; (d) a `.contest` file written for a different tool_input leaves this call judged and denied; (e) a `Write` whose file_path lies under `<TMPDIR>/guardrail-contest/` exits 0 with no deny and the stub is not called. Against the worker at dd055a7b (a) finds no path in the reason and (b) is denied, so the cases fail there.
UNRECORDED: with GUARD_CONTEST_LOG naming a path beneath a regular file, the contested fire of (b) still exits 0 with no deny, and its notice says the contest was not recorded.

SAME PAYLOAD: in the architect's scope, the payload the worker emits under STANCE_EMIT_PAYLOAD for an `Edit` of packages/forge/src/x.ts and for a `Task` to implementer carrying `install of guided-install` is byte-identical from the worker at dd055a7b and at the landed commit; print each pair's cksum.
LEAN: `wc -c < packages/canon/targets/guardrail/purview-guardrail.sh` prints at most 8192 (15407 at dd055a7b); print it.

ONE HOME: packages/canon/src/guard-shell.ts exports judgePayloadCapBytes, judgeClipShell and contestShell; `grep -n 'stance-guardrail.js' packages/canon/src/hooks/purview-guardrail.ts packages/canon/test/purview-guardrail.test.ts` prints nothing (2 lines at dd055a7b); print both counts.
After the commit, `pnpm canon:project:targets` leaves `git status --porcelain packages/canon/targets` empty.

Green: `pnpm --filter @cratylus/canon exec vitest run test/purview-guardrail.test.ts test/hook-rule-boundary.test.ts test/reader-density.test.ts test/harness-independence.test.ts test/architecture.test.ts` and `pnpm --filter @cratylus/canon typecheck` exit 0.
`git diff --name-only <the unit's base> <landed commit>` lists only paths in this unit's outputs (records/ excepted).
